content.value: This document provides a complete guide for integrating the Character Customization System (v1.2) into your Unreal Engine projects. It is designed for modularity, using interface-driven communication and decomposed widgets to ensure effortless integration and extension.
Support: For questions or assistance, please leave a comment on the product page or join the Discord server for faster resolution. Please consider rating and reviewing the asset if it proves useful.

• Modular Design:
    • The system is heavily interface-driven.
    • Widgets are decomposed into reusable elements to unify style and logic across different screens.
    • The system is decoupled from the Character Selection System to maintain modularity and reduce complexity.
• GameMode Logic: The BP_GM_CharCustomSystem GameMode handles the management of on-screen widgets (creation, removal, and updates) .
• GameInstance: The BP_CustomizationGameInstance customisation persistence across levels.
• Copy or Migrate entire CharacterCustomizationSystem folder to your project.
• Copy the functions in FunctionToCopy category inside BP_Char01 into your character blueprint - addNewAccessoryComponent, removeCurrentAccessoryComponent and updateCustomisationData.
• Implement BPI_PlayerInterface in your character blueprint.

• Implement the functions in category CCS | Core for customisation features. For full integration including the menu and the camera, see BP_Char01 and re-implement all the interface functions in your character blueprint.
• You will need to create new variables. Right click on any missing variable and then select PromoteToVariable.
• On the EventBeginPlay, call UpdateCustomisationData.
• If you only wish to integrate character customization only, create an input event that creates the character customization screen widget - W_Customisation.
• For full integration, add gameplayCamera component to your character and in the asset properties, select - CA_CBP.
• Then, in the worldSettings for the level, select - BP_GM_CharCustomSystem.
• Set DefaultPawnClass to your character blueprint class.
• Make sure your character skeleton has all the required sockets for adding customisation items.

value: <ul>
• Go inside Blueprints > Data folder and duplicate any existing data asset.
• Open the data asset and click on the trash icon to empty the AttachmentData.
• Click the plus icon to add a new element in the map.
• The default value will be none. Click on it and select your desired category - Face, Torso, Legs or Shoes.
• Expand the section and click on plus icon to add items in that category.
• Always keep the first item in any category empty. This indicates the no attachments state for the character during the customization process.
<li>In the next item, fill the appropriate data -
<ul>
• isSkeletalMesh: Determines if or not the item to be attached to the character is a skeletal mesh or a static mesh.
• SkeletalMesh: If this item is a skeletal mesh, i.e. isSkeletalMesh is set to true, then select your desired mesh.
• AnimBPSkeletalMesh: If this skeletal mesh has its own animation blueprint, then select it here or leave it empty.
• UseMasterPose: Set this to true if you want this item to follow and character's animation data like clothing assets, else leave it false.
• StaticMesh: Select your static mesh asset if this item is not a skeletal mesh.

• AttachmentCategory: Select the category of this item. This category should be carefully set. The category of the map is used by the widget screen but the inside category is used by the player character.
• SocketName: The socket to which this item will be attached. If UseMasterPose is set to true, then leave it None.
• ItemDescription: This field can be used to write about the item's lore, defining features or properties.
<ul>
<li>The system uses a component-based camera manager on the character blueprint.</li
• States: Controls properties for MainMenu, Selection, and Gameplay.
• Rigs: Specific Data Assets defining camera behavior for each state.
The system uses BPI_PlayerInterface across multiple classes:
• Widget: Receives messages to disable buttons.
• GameMode: Handles construction/deconstruction of widgets.
• Character: Receives input availability messages.
Ensure your blueprint inherits from the standard Character class and implements BPI_PlayerInterface.
Add the BPC_PlayerAttributes component to store CustomizationData data assets.

Q: Can I combine this with the Character Selection System?
A: Yes, but this asset is designed as standalone to reduce complexity. You will need to manually merge the logic if you require both systems in a single GameMode/Controller.

Q: Why is my new customization category not showing?
A: Ensure you have added the category to the E_AttachmentPoints enumeration and updated the button properties in the UI widget to match the category name exactly.

Q: How do I set a default 'None' option?
A: When adding elements to your Data Asset (DA_PDA_UE5), leave the first element empty. This acts as the default 'unequipped' state.
